grh_57431b74a4bd5ab3d99b.title: The Dishonest Boy
paragraphs: Russell Brandt steals his poor report card before his parents can see it and tries to shift suspicion onto Ira Nelson, his father's elderly longtime bookkeeper. The lie becomes dangerous because Mr. Brandt has already been considering dismissing Ira as no longer useful to the business. Dr. Christian questions Russell closely, catches the contradictions in his story and forces him to admit that he took the report card and falsely accused Ira. When Russell finally confesses, Dr. Christian reminds his angry father that honesty and courage are learned rather than automatic, and that Russell's lie did not create the father's willingness to discard a loyal old employee. The boy is held accountable, but his decision to tell the truth becomes the beginning of making things right.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on April 17, 1938. It is listed as episode 24 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Robert Mitchell, The St. Branden's Boys Choir, and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Art Gilmore as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 31 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_57462cdd6925af0d3e9d.title: Live Forever
paragraphs: A man terrified of death is carried in a vision into a future where science has made human beings effectively immortal. Instead of paradise, he finds an overcrowded society dominated forever by the same ancient people, while younger generations have no work, authority or purpose. A group of frustrated young immortals recruits him into assassinating their elders to make room for themselves, and the horror sends him back to his own time newly convinced that death is necessary for life and renewal.

paragraphs: John Unger visits the impossibly wealthy Washington family and discovers that their fortune comes from a mountain-sized diamond whose existence must be kept secret at any cost. Guests who learn too much are imprisoned or killed, and Braddock Washington plans to murder John despite his daughter Kismine's love for him. grh_57493446eed7f62230cd.title: Melody Ranch - Idaho
paragraphs: Following the opening song 'Idaho,' Gene investigates why cattle on young Betty Carson's ranch are mysteriously dying. Dead grass beside the ranch's salt blocks leads to laboratory tests showing that the blocks were poisoned with arsenic made tasteless in the salt. Gene discovers that Betty's guardian, Uncle Dan Carson, has been pretending to be crippled; he is poisoning the herd to force a sale before Betty turns twenty-one because a new railroad spur will make the property highly valuable. A distinctive footprint from Dan's leg brace helps expose the deception, and his attempt to silence Gene and Betty ends with him being taken for prosecution.
